selected.title: Researchers made a tiny, lightning-like glowing sphere in a lab
selected.summary: A new experiment produced a short-lived glowing structure that researchers say may offer a controlled way to study soliton physics and the long-standing mystery of ball lightning.
selected.why_it_matters: A repeatable laboratory setup could help separate what scientists can reproduce from what eyewitness reports describe in nature.
selected.challenge_question: What did the researchers create in the laboratory?
selected.answer_explanation: The study reports a controlled, long-lived soliton-like glowing structure. It may help investigate ball lightning, but it does not establish that the natural phenomenon has been fully recreated.
selected.butterfly_question: How can recreating a rare natural event in a lab help explain what people see outdoors?
